newsitem.title: INDIA: India calls for demilitarisation of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: India calls for demilitarisation of Kabul.

text.p: India reiterated its support for ousted Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani on Wednesday and called for the demilitarisation of Kabul as a condition for the pursuit of peace in Afghanistan.

Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said in a statement to parliament that the government was following events very closely in Afghanistan, where the Taleban militia overran the capital Kabul on September 27.

"The pursuit of obscurantist doctrine by the Taleban leadership and the consequent denial of human rights, especially the rights of women, have been extensively condemned," he said, noting the risk of an adverse impact on India's security.
He said New Delhi had maintained contact with "the legitimate Afghan government, led by President Rabbani", noting that Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda met Rabbani recently in Rome.
An Indian delegation led by a senior Foreign Ministry official met General Abdul Rashid Dostum in his stronghold of Mazar-i-Sharif on November 10, Gujral said.
Dostum, who runs six of Afghanistan's 33 provinces, is allied with Rabbani's forces.
Gujral said India's position on Afghanistan called for a cessation of foreign interference and arms supply.

"There could be no military solution," he said. "The cessation of violence and armed hostilities and the demilitarisation of Kabul would provide the right conditions for the political process. These should be actively pursued."
The Indian foreign minister said New Delhi was "greatly disturbed and distressed at the denial of human rights, especially those of women, which have been recently witnessed in Afghanistan".

Citing media reports of the Taleban handing over "terrorist training facilities" to the Pakistan-based Harkat-ul-Ansar militant group, Gujral said Pakistani and other youths were reportedly being trained there for "terrorist activities" in Kashmir.
India accuses Pakistan, which rules over one third of Kashmir, of arming and training guerrillas fighting Indian rule in Jammu and Kashmir state. Islamabad denies the claim.
Gujral said the Indian government would maintain its vigilance and take all necessary steps to safeguard the country's security.
